name: Karl G. Jansky Very Large Array
place: Plains of San Agustin, near Socorro, New Mexico
description: A centimeter-wavelength radio observatory of 28 dishes, 25 m each (27 in use at a time), arranged in a Y shape and operated as one interferometer. It is run by the National Radio Astronomy Observatory.
highlights: Construction began in April 1973 and the array was formally inaugurated in 1980.
Astronomers have used it for key observations of black holes and protoplanetary disks, and to find magnetic filaments at the Milky Way's centre.
film: The VLA is a filming location of Contact (1997), the film of Carl Sagan's novel about a radio signal from another star.
